newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish budget vote likely late on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Polish budget vote likely late on Friday.

text.p: Poland's lower house of parliament is likely to vote on the 1997 national budget draft late on Friday, the parliament's press office said.
The press office quoted house speaker Jozef Zych as saying he would do all he could to bring the bill to vote on Friday rather than at a session next week.
The vote will be held next week if the budgetary committee fails to finish work on the numerous amendments proposed on Wednesday when the bill's second reading began, the office said.
The ruling leftist coalition of ex-communists and a peasant party, controlling a firm majority in parliament, should easily pass the draft, seen as a continuation of last year's budget.
The budget will then have to clear the Senate and be signed by President Aleksander Kwasniewski, who is not expected to oppose the bill.
The bill provides for slightly higher revenues and spending levels than in 1996 and a deficit amounting to 2.8 percent of gross domestic product, compared with 2.5 percent last year.
